verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A faster insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

The particulate figures are partly fabricated: "gaps entered at the permit limit, and a quarter of scheduled runs at each stack returned no reading" means 25 percent of the data is a substituted fixed value rather than a measurement, so the 8-14 percent drops could be driven by how many gaps each quarter had rather than by actual emissions.

The denominator is narrower than the claim: "Rates cover the patients discharged from each ward, and each ward transferred out a quarter of those admitted." A quarter of admitted patients - plausibly the sickest, most infection-prone ones - are excluded from the ward infection rate entirely.

Revenue per order is measured on a narrower population than the claim: "Figures cover the orders that cleared the staffed tills, and about a fifth of each store's orders went through self-checkout." Roughly 20 percent of orders are excluded, and self-checkout baskets differ systematically in size, so the 4-7 percent rise need not hold for revenue per order overall.

The germination figures are partly imputed: "unscored ones counted as nil, and about a fifth of each lot's trays went unscored." A fifth of trays are scored zero without being observed, so a 6-11 point gap against the previous sowing can be produced by a difference in unscored fractions rather than by the coating.

Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the intervention began: cohort One "started 4 April; by 29 March resting heart rate ran 5 bpm below", and cohort Three "started 5 October; by 30 September ... 6 bpm below". The drop is dated prior to enrollment, so the app cannot have caused it.
